title: Find missing number in an array
stepTitle: Solve Problems on Arrays [Easy -> Medium -> Hard]
category: Solve Problems on Arrays [Easy -> Medium -> Hard]
problemStatement: An array holds n distinct numbers from 1..n+1 with exactly one missing. Find it.
intuition: Compare the array against what it should have been. Sum difference or XOR cancellation both isolate the missing value in one pass with O(1) memory.

approaches.title: Brute: search for each candidate
approaches.idea: For every value 1..N, scan the array.

approaches.title: Better: hash set
approaches.idea: Membership in O(1), at the cost of O(n) memory.

approaches.title: Optimal: sum difference (or XOR)
approaches.idea: expected - actual. XOR avoids any overflow concern in fixed-width languages.
approaches.whyWorks: XOR is its own inverse, so every present value cancels and only the missing one survives.

edgeCases: Overflow in C++/Java for large n (prefer XOR)
commonMistakes: Using n instead of n+1 in the formula
patternRecognition: "Exactly one element differs from a known multiset" -> sum or XOR cancellation
followUps: Which is safer in Java: sum or XOR, and why?
interviewInsight: Offer both formulas and name the overflow trade-off — that is the differentiator here.
